children.translated_text: <s>Kauthuma Gṛhyasūtra</s>

children.text: KauthGS 1:
children.translated_text: <s>Kauthuma Gṛhyasūtra</s>, Chapter 1:

children.text:
athātaḥ prāyaścittāni /
athātaḥ kramāṇāṃ vadaye gṛhastho vā brahmacārī vā gṛhastho gṛhāgnau brahmacārī laukikāgnau gṛhasyeṣviticaraṇena paricaraṇe vā brahmacaryavicchinne laukikāgnau prātarāhutipūrvakaṃ naimittikaṃ kāryaṃm /
punarādhāne varjayet sāyamupakramya tātkālikaprāyaścittāpattau cettābhyāṃ tatra kāryam /
paurṇamyāhutyāmatītaṃ cettābhyāṃ tattatkuryuḥ parvaṇā cetsaṃkalya kāryam tadabhāve sadyaḥ kuryād apareṇa darśaṃ tve prāyaścittiḥ trirātraṃ pañcarātraṃ vā dadharātrāttāḥ prāyaścittapūrvayajña yajete tāvubhau parvā saṃkalya tītau tāmiṣṭau tadvat tatra yadi lopaṃ vā taṃ māmāsādatītaṃ vā punarādhānaṃ kuryuḥ /

prāyaścittārthe prājāpatyaṃ vā tadūrdhvaṃ viśeṣaśca gṛhāgnau gṛhyāgniṃ yadi sparśettaṃtra ta meko vā kāryo mantrāṇāṃ tāvubhau brūyāttaṃtrī tatsamidho saṃyuktaṃ gṛhṇan navarohaṇaṃ tataḥ karma prāṇāyāmaṃ kuryuḥ /
children.translated_text: For the purpose of expiation, the <s>Prājāpatya</s> [penance] or what is beyond that [should be performed]. And the specific [rule] regarding the domestic fire: if one should touch the <s>gṛhyāgni</s> (domestic sacred fire), then one [oblation] should be made there. For the <s>mantras</s>, both should be recited. The ritual procedure, together with the fuel-sticks, should be performed in conjunction. [One should perform] the re-ascent (<s>navarohaṇa</s>); after that, they should perform the ritual action and <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control).

children.text: tūṣṇīṃ pariṣicya mantreṇābhyarvyāhutyāmanartha staras tāvubho dvau samidhamādhāya bhaṣatkarmāṃ mantraṃ brūyāt /
children.translated_text: Having silently sprinkled, and having offered the oblation with the <s>mantra</s>, [being] without purpose [other than expiation] — both those two, having placed two fuel-sticks, should recite the <s>bhaṣat</s>-rite <s>mantra</s>.

children.text: atra pupastūṣṇīṃ kāryaṃ patnī vā iti samānaṃ samāropaṇaṃ kuryuḥ kartavyā iti vaitadu bhavati svayaṃ svayaṃ prāyaścittī tata ūrdhvaṃ viśeṣaṃ syād anyāgno svayamamasmadbhāvi tathāci yajñidknevarohaṇaṃ kuryāṃ ādisamāropaṇaṃ prajñātastadamavrimutsṛjya bhūrbhuvaḥ svariti brūyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Here the offering should be done silently, or the wife [may do it] — thus the re-ascent procedure is the same. They should perform it. This is what is to be done — thus it becomes so. Each one individually [is] the performer of expiation. After that, there should be a specific [rite]. In another fire, it should happen by oneself. And thus one should perform the re-ascent for the sacrificial [fire]. Having understood the initial re-ascent procedure, having released that, one should recite "<s>bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ</s>" (earth, atmosphere, heaven).

children.text: tūṣṇīṃ tiṣṭhan na gacchet tadagnipatyāṃ ta prāpnau karmabhraṣṭā svagṛhyāgnau svayaṃ svayaṃ prāyaścittir ata ūrdhvaṃ viśeṣaṃ syādājyatantrairanāropaṇaṃ cetsamāropaṇaṃ prājñātaḥ punarārabhya prāyarāhutyādi prapadāntaparyantaṃ yatkiṃcitkarma yadi lopaṃ syāt prātarāhutiścetprāyaścittamityeke nyūnākarmādi punarāvṛttiḥ pradhānādūrdhvaṃ prāyaścittir ata ūrdhvaṃ viśeṣaścarutantreṇa tato vyākhyātā prāgudakpravaṇe deśe tatra sthaṃḍisamupali yāt // KauthGS_1 //
children.translated_text: Standing silently, one should not go. In that fire-ritual, the performers of the rite who have fallen from their duties [should perform expiation] in their own <s>gṛhyāgni</s> (domestic fire), each one individually performing expiation. After that, there should be a specific [rite]. If there is no re-ascent in the <s>ājya</s>-rituals (ghee oblation procedures), the re-ascent should be done by one who understands. Having begun again from the morning oblation up to the <s>prapada</s>-rite, if there is any omission in whatever rite, if it is the morning oblation, that itself is the expiation — say some. For deficient rites, there is repetition. After the main [rite], the expiation [follows]. After that, the specific [rule] is explained through the <s>caru</s>-ritual (oblation of cooked grain) procedure. In a place sloping toward the north and east, there one should prepare the ground-altar (<s>sthaṇḍila</s>).

Now, therefore, the expiatory rites (<s>prāyaścitta</s>).
Now, therefore, I shall state the procedures: whether a householder (<s>gṛhastha</s>) or a celibate student (<s>brahmacārī</s>) — the householder [performs] in the domestic fire (<s>gṛhāgni</s>), the brahmacārī in an ordinary fire (<s>laukikāgni</s>). In the householder's [rites], the service is performed according to the school's practice. When the <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship) is broken, the occasional (<s>naimittika</s>) rite should be performed in the ordinary fire, preceded by the morning oblation (<s>prātarāhuti</s>).
In the re-establishment of the fire (<s>punarādhāna</s>), one should omit [the evening rite]; having begun in the evening, if a lapse requiring immediate expiation occurs, it should be done with those two [fires]. If the full-moon oblation has passed, they should perform that respective [rite] with those two. If a <s>parvan</s> (juncture day) [has passed], it should be done with a formal resolve (<s>saṃkalpa</s>). In its absence, one should perform it immediately. After the new-moon day, however, the expiation [requires] three nights or five nights. After that period, one should perform the sacrifice preceded by the expiation. Both those two <s>parvan</s> [rites], having made a resolve — if they have passed, one should perform those desired [rites] likewise. If there is an omission, or that has passed beyond recall, one should perform the re-establishment of the fire.

children.text: KauthGS 2:
children.translated_text: <s>Kauthuma Gṛhyasūtra</s>, Chapter 2:

children.text:
athātaḥ prāṅmukho bhūtvodagagreṣu darbheṣu omityuccairupaviśya gṛhāgnau nirīkṣyamāṇollekhanaṃ tataḥ kārayet /
tatprātarāhutiṃ hutvā vedavidbrāhmaṇaṃ labhet tadalābhe khādiranyāyaḥ chatraguttarāsaṃ ceti khādiraṃ nyā ityeke brāhmaṇaṃ prārthayet /
brāhmaṇaṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ bṛhaspatirbrahmāhaṃ mānuṣa iti brūyāt ācāryo dve darbhāgna dadyāt brāhmaṇo nirastaḥ parāvasuriti dakṣiṇāstṛṇaṃ nirasyāsanārthe prāgagrāndarbhānāstīryā vasoḥ sadane sīdāmotyudaṅmukha omityupāṃśuruviśed ācāryo brāhmaṇamarcayitvā tataḥ kāṃsyapātramādāya mṛnmayapātraṃ vābhidyam tāmravarjaṃ rajata iti śālitaṇḍulānnavaśūrpeṇādāyodagudvāsyo nirvāpārthena sakṛtpātraṃ pūrayet /
dvistūṣṇīṃ kāryamo prokṣyāmīti brūyād āpaḥ prāvayantyudagudvāsya tataḥ samūhanādyājyatantreṣu gṛhyokte navaparvaṇaṃ kāryaṃ tatpātnamutthāpyāgnimadhye sthāpyo nirvāpa iti brūyāt tadā jīvasaṇḍulān śrapayet /
sruveṇābhighāryāgnerbahistaraṇādaṃtayorudagudvāsya punaḥ prokṣaṇaṃ kuryāt /
tata idhmamādāya tatra viśeṣaḥ samidhamucyace /
bahvacāḥ khādireṇa bodhāyanāḥ palāśeśchandogāḥ udajumbareṇa yajante /
children.translated_text: The followers of <s>Bahvṛca</s> (Ṛgvedins) [use] <s>khadira</s> wood; the followers of <s>Bodhāyana</s> [use] <s>palāśa</s> (Butea monosperma); the <s>Chandogas</s> (Sāmavedins) sacrifice with <s>udumbara</s> (Ficus racemosa) wood.

children.text: prādeśamātrāḥ kaśapṛṣṭhāḥ samāgratoguṃṣṭhaparvaghṛtadyumātroḥ prajñātāgrāḥ kārayitvā tadabhāve darbhairvā saptadaśaiḥ ādāya anaṣṭārthamekaṃ prapadārthamekamidhmārthe pacadaśam etāni saptadaśa gṛhṇan sruveṇābhighārya agramavyamūlonyanuyājārthamuttarato nidhāya paṃcadaśamagno prakṣipya śeṣeṇa prapadaṃ jape yāvacīriti śaṭhāntāni tāvatsvāṣaso dhārayanta rūpāhanagnau hutvā śeṣākṣatānabhyarcya tato vyāhṛtibhiḥ tisṛbhiḥ hutvā tato kāmajavyāhṛkī ca hutvā cakṣuṣī caturgṛhītaṃ sruveṇa juhuyāt /
children.translated_text: Having had [sacrificial blades] made, [each] a span in length, with backs like a tortoise shell, with known tips the size of a thumb-joint smeared with ghee, or in their absence, having taken seventeen <s>darbha</s> grasses — one for the offering of the foot, one for the purpose of fuel, fifteen for the after-offerings — grasping these seventeen, having sprinkled [them] with the <s>sruva</s> (ladle), having placed aside to the north the tip portions with roots below for the purpose of the after-offerings, having cast the fifteenth into the fire, with the remainder one should recite for the foot-offering as far as 'until it is worn out,' ending with the <s>śaṭha</s> [formula]. For that many [recitations], holding one's own portion, having offered into the fire after the day, having honored the remaining grains, then having offered with the three <s>Vyāhṛtis</s> ('Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ'), and then having offered the <s>Kāmaja-vyāhṛti</s> as well, one should offer the <s>Cakṣuṣī</s> [oblation] taken four times with the <s>sruva</s>.

children.text: eteṣāṃ carutantre eteṣāṃ yathārthaṃ syāt tatra viśeṣastu varadānaprayogocyate /
children.translated_text: In the system of <s>caru</s> (oblation) rituals, these should be [performed] according to their purposes. The specific difference, however, is stated in the procedure for the granting of boons.

children.text: khādiranyāyena ca gṛhyokteḥ kuthumasya mathādityuktvā kauthumo kuthumasya mārgamācarati // KauthGS_2 //
children.translated_text: And according to the rule of the <s>Khādira</s> [Gṛhyasūtra], as stated in the Gṛhya [texts]: having declared 'of <s>Kuthuma</s>,' the <s>Kauthuma</s> [school] follows the path of <s>Kuthuma</s>. (KauthGS 2)

Now, therefore, facing east, having sat down on <s>darbha</s> grass with tips pointing north, saying "<s>Om</s>" aloud, while looking at the domestic fire (<s>gṛhāgni</s>), one should then have the marking [of the ground] done.
Then, having offered the morning oblation, one should obtain a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> learned in the <s>Vedas</s>. If unavailable, the rule of <s>khadira</s> (Acacia catechu) wood [applies] — along with an umbrella and an upper garment — thus [some say] the <s>khadira</s> is the standard; others say one should request a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
One should address the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [saying]: "<s>Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, I am a human." The teacher should give two <s>darbha</s> [blades] to the fire. The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, [saying] "Cast out, <s>Parāvasu</s>," should discard the southern grass to the right, and for the seat, having spread <s>darbha</s> with tips pointing east, should sit facing north [saying] "In the seat of <s>Vasu</s>, I sit down," saying "<s>Om</s>" softly. The teacher, having honored the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, should then take a bronze vessel — or an earthen vessel, avoiding copper, [or] silver. Taking <s>śāli</s>-rice grains with a new winnowing basket, with [their tips] pointing north, one should fill the vessel once for the purpose of offering (<s>nirvāpa</s>).
Twice, [this] should be done silently, saying "I shall sprinkle" (<s>prokṣyāmi</s>). "The waters flow forth" — [saying this], with [tips] pointing north, then from the sweeping onward, in the <s>ājya</s>-ritual procedures as stated in the <s>Gṛhya</s> [sūtra], the nine-juncture rite should be performed. The cooking-vessel, having been raised, should be placed in the middle of the fire, saying "<s>nirvāpa</s>" (offering). Then one should cook the living grains [i.e., unhusked rice].
Having poured ghee with the <s>sruva</s> (ladle) and placed [the grains] outside the fire on the spreading-grass with [tips] pointing north, one should perform the sprinkling again.
Then, taking the fuel-stick — here is the specific [rule]: it is called a <s>samidh</s> (fuel-stick).

children.text: KauthGS 3:
children.translated_text: KauthGS 3:

children.text: athātaḥ carupātraṃ nirīkṣya saṃmukhe sthāpanaṃ kāryam udagugvāsya ityeke saṃmukhe kāryaḥ carordvibhāgaṃ kāryaṃ sruvapātramāsādya cchidvānārdaṃ tadabhāve kāṃsyapātraṃ vā tanmadhye 'bhighārya caroḥ pūrvadeśe sakṛdavadāya dvitīyye madhyame hyavadānaṃ śeṣe sruvapātre punaścābhidhārya agnimadhye juhuyāt tvadvitīyaṃ ceñcaroḥ paścimadeśe syātsakṛ0vadāya dvibhighāryā prāgudagdeśe juguyayāj jāmadagnyāścenmavyat paścāt purastāta sakṛdavadāya bhṛguṇā madhyame kārṣmaryastatra carūṇāmuṣmāṇāṃ kriyate apalanayedyayorojaseti dvistūṣṇīṃ kuryātkarmagnyāvupahatiścetprā jāpatyaṃ vā prāyaścittaṃ juhuyāt /
children.translated_text: Now then, having inspected the <s>caru</s> (oblation) vessel, it should be placed facing [the officiant]. Some say facing north. The upper portion of the <s>caru</s> should be prepared. Having procured the <s>sruva</s> vessel, [one uses] a split [wooden] vessel; in its absence, a bronze vessel may be used. Having sprinkled [ghee] in the middle of that, one should take a portion once from the eastern side of the <s>caru</s>, a second portion from the middle, and the remainder [should be placed] in the <s>sruva</s> vessel. Having sprinkled again, one should offer in the middle of the fire. And if a second [offering is needed], from the western side of the <s>caru</s>, one should take a portion once, sprinkle twice, and offer toward the northeast direction. If [the sacrificer is] of the <s>Jāmadagnya</s> [lineage], [the offering is] of barley — first from behind, then from the front, taking a portion once; [if] of the <s>Bhṛgu</s> [lineage], from the middle; for the <s>Kārṣmarya</s>, in the case of those <s>caru</s> oblations, the heating is done. One should remove [the remainder] with [the mantra] 'by vigor' (<s>ojasā</s>). Twice one should perform silently. If there is an error in the ritual fire, one should offer a <s>Prājāpatya</s> expiation.

children.text: atītavicchinne tatkṣaṇe ṣaṣṭirdevatā hutvā ca tad ahorātramatītaṃ dramasauryaṣu ityeteṣu parvādyai svāmimavyame cetkartavyaṃ syāt prāyaścittir gṛhyāgnau karma kartumapi vāṇicaturthe rajaścāḍālānanugate vā saṃvatsarādūrdhvaṃ yathākṛcchraṃ vapanaṃ ca tathā prāyaścitti prāyaścittiḥ // KauthGS_3 //
children.translated_text: When [the ritual] has lapsed and been interrupted, at that very moment, having offered to the sixty deities, and if that day-and-night has passed, [one should perform the rite] in the <s>Dram</s>, <s>Saurya</s>, and similar [periods] — on the <s>parvan</s> (juncture) days. If the principal [rite] needs to be performed, there is an expiation. Even to perform a rite on the domestic fire (<s>gṛhyāgni</s>), or on the fourth [day] of menstruation, or when followed by a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> — after a year, according to the severity, shaving [of the head should be performed], and likewise the expiation. (KauthGS 3)

children.text: KauthGS 4:
children.translated_text: KauthGS 4:

children.text: atha parvaprāyaścittire udagayanaṃ vā dakṣiṇāyanaṃ vā vasantādyādiṣaṣṭhe caturṇāṃ cāndramāsasaurya ityeteṣu parvādyaignāmiṣṭamadhye cetkartavyaṃ syātprāyaścittir gṛhyāgnau karmārtumapi pāṇicaturthehani tvadārabhya tanmā gādanta udayana dakṣiṇāgnau ceṣṭātkartavya tanmāsādisaṃkalpaiḥ kartavyaṃ syātprāyaścittir vivāhe yadi pūrvapakṣe cedapare paurṇamāsyaidārabhya kartavyaḥ syāt saṃkalpairdaśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ dvāviṣṭara ityuktau tatra dvitīyā viṣṭedinā vyādā yajñe 'narthaḥ tasmāttābhyāṃ dvāviṣṭauropaṃ vighnaṃ kartavyaṃ syātprāyaścitti ni tisṛbhiścāvamārayāni tāṃ svadhā me viṣṭimadhyā cetkartavyaṃ syātprāyaścittir anayorāghānamadhye rāhuparvaṇi caindrapamāha iti /
children.translated_text: Now regarding the expiation for [missed] <s>parvan</s> (juncture) rites: whether [during] the northern course [of the sun] or the southern course, in the six [seasons] beginning with spring, and in the four [types of months] — lunar, solar, and the rest — on those <s>parvan</s> days, if a rite among the desired ones needs to be performed, there is an expiation [to be done] on the domestic fire (<s>gṛhyāgni</s>). Even on the fourth day after [the beginning of menstruation], commencing from that [time], one should proceed until that month's end. If [the rite falls during] the northern or southern [solstice] course, it should be performed with the appropriate monthly resolutions. There is an expiation for [an interruption in] a marriage: if [it falls] in the bright fortnight, [one should begin] from the other [dark] fortnight; if on the full moon, it should be performed [starting from that]. With resolutions for the ten new-moon and full-moon [rites], two spreading-grasses (<s>viṣṭara</s>) are prescribed. There, the second [is to be placed] on the <s>viṣṭi</s> day. In the sacrifice, [any omission would be] harmful; therefore, with those two, the double spreading-grass should be prepared as an obstacle-remedy. There should be an expiation with the three [verses beginning] 'may the <s>Avamāra</s> [deities protect].' [If the interruption falls] in the middle of a <s>viṣṭi</s>, there should be an expiation. In the middle of these fire-installations, and during the <s>Rāhu</s> eclipse, [the formula] 'of <s>Indra</s>' is declared.

children.text: ādyapaṅkau dvitīyā gāyatryāṃ ubhayayordevatā candra ityuktvā prāyaścittiḥ /
children.translated_text: In the first section, [and] in the second with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> [meter], the deity of both is <s>Candra</s> (the Moon) — thus having declared, [there is] an expiation.

children.text: sauryaḥ parvaṇi ceccitraṃ devānāmudu tyāmitya ādyaiḥ triṣṭup ta dvitīye gāyatrī vā ubhayordevatā sūrya ityuktvā prāyaścittiḥ prāyaścittaṃ vinā punaścārambhiṇiṃ cet kartavyaṃ syātprāyaścittis tāṃ saṃkalpya madhye śrāddhakarmāṇi tatrāgnau karaṇaṃ kapāṇau hutaṃ vā tadvad bhuñjānaḥ kartavyaṃ syātprāyaścir atha viśeṣaśca niyamairdampatyormadhye rajaścāṇḍālagamane vā kartavyaṃ syātprāyaścittis tayorādhānamadhye rāśau madhye sparśakṣayaṃ vā vṛddhi vā kartavyaṃ syātprāyaścittis tayorādhāmamadhye 'nyagrāmaṃ praviśya patho gatvā kratavyaṃ syātprāyaścittistayormadhye ubhāvanyagamane vā divā maithune vā kartavyaṃ syātprāyaścittiḥ puruṣo bhojanamadhye tathā karma maithunaṃ ca śvānamārjālā saṃspṛṣṭvā kartavyaṃ syātprāyaścittir atha viśeṣaśca gṛhyāvanagnikānāṃ ca vidhavāṃ spṛṣṭvā kartavyaṃ syātprāyaścittir aśroyī śūdrāntabhogo cārvāko paradārābhigamano svakarmatyāgo nityaṃ parānnabhojo tathānagrāho gobrahmaṇavadhi veśyātkuṭumbī rājānnabhojo adhyāpanagraṃthatyāgo vidyādūṣyaguruvādai prāṇasaṃhārī mārjālocchiṣṭabhojī vedavikrayo kanyāpativratādūṣī svakuṭumbatyāgī upādhyāyagurordūṣo guroḥ patnyābhigamanī māṃsabhakṣī śrāddhakālatyāgī tathā śrāddhabhojī taṭhākasaṃhārī varṣavardhī sadārāgo brāhmaṇatāḍo mṛttikāpāṣāṇatāhī sadocchaṣṭo vipradūṣo iti te caṃḍālasamāḥ gṛhyāgnau spṛṣṭā daṃpatyorvāsacelaṃ kāryaṃ kartavyaṃ syātprāyaścitti prāyaścittārthe ṣaṣṭhidevatā uktā /
children.translated_text: The solar [rite]: if at a <s>parvan</s> (junction day), [one should recite] 'citraṃ devānām' and so forth — the first [verse] is in <s>triṣṭubh</s> meter, the second in <s>gāyatrī</s> or [either]; the deity of both is <s>Sūrya</s>. Having declared thus, the <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation) [follows]. Without expiation, if one must perform the rite again from the beginning, the expiation should be resolved upon; in the middle [one performs] <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral) rites. Therein, the offering is made in the fire, or offered in the hand — likewise while eating, the expiation should be performed. Now the specifics: with observances, if during [the period] between the couple, [there occurs] menstruation or contact with a <s>caṇḍāla</s>, the expiation should be performed; during their fire-establishment, during the [planetary] conjunction, if there is loss of contact or increase, the expiation should be performed; during their fire-establishment, if entering another village or going on a journey, the expiation should be performed; between the two, if either has intercourse with another or [there is] daytime intercourse, the expiation should be performed. If a man, during eating, [performs] such a rite or intercourse, or having touched a dog or a cat, the expiation should be performed. Now the specifics for those with and without the <s>gṛhya</s> (domestic) fire: having touched a widow, the expiation should be performed. [The following are considered equal to caṇḍālas:] one who does not listen [to the Vedas], one who enjoys [the company of] <s>Śūdra</s>s, a <s>Cārvāka</s> (materialist), one who approaches another's wife, one who abandons his own duties, one who constantly eats another's food, likewise one who does not accept [what is proper], a killer of cows or <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, a householder [who frequents] prostitutes, one who eats royal food, one who abandons teaching and scripture, one who harms life through corrupting knowledge and slandering the teacher, one who eats the leftovers of a cat, one who sells the <s>Veda</s>s, one who corrupts a maiden or a faithful wife, one who abandons his own family, one who insults the preceptor or teacher, one who approaches the teacher's wife, a meat-eater, one who abandons [rites] at the time of <s>śrāddha</s>, likewise one who eats at a <s>śrāddha</s> [improperly], a destroyer of reservoirs, one who increases the rains [through sorcery], one always attached to [another's] wife, a striker of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, a striker with clods or stones, one always [eating] leftovers, a reviler of <s>Vipra</s>s (learned Brāhmaṇas) — these are equal to <s>caṇḍāla</s>s. If [such persons are] touched near the domestic fire, the couple should wash their garments; the expiation should be performed. For the purpose of expiation, the deity of the sixth [day] is prescribed.

children.text: kanyahṛtīni vyāhṛtibhistṛsṛbhiḥ āvṛttiḥ punaśca tisṛbhirdvādaśaguṇaṃ kāryaṃ prājāpatyaṃ na pañcakasamastāntaṃ --ri pāhi no agrayenase iti tisṛbhiḥ prājāpatyamekaṃ yatkusīdaṃ ca samastāntaṃ caturthī sviṣṭakṛdvā ityeṣāṃ prāyaścittirkaṃ evaṃ brāhmaṇeyo yāsāḥ prāyaścittāṃ vikataṃ jānanyaḥ śarīrādvimucyate yaḥ śarīrādvimucyate // KauthGS_4 //
children.translated_text: The maiden-taking [rites]: with the three <s>vyāhṛti</s>s (sacred utterances), repetition; and again with three, twelve-fold it should be done. The <s>Prājāpatya</s> (penance dedicated to <s>Prajāpati</s>) [is performed]; not ending with a group of five — 'pāhi naḥ' ('protect us') and 'agrayā nase' — with these three, one <s>Prājāpatya</s>; and 'yat kusīdam' (whatever usury) ending with the complete [verse]; the fourth is <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (the fire-offering for proper completion). Thus is the expiation for these. In this way, a son of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, knowing these expiations in full, is freed from the body; [indeed] he is freed from the body.

children.text: KauthGS 5:
children.translated_text: <s>Kauthuma Gṛhyasūtra</s>, Section 5:

children.text: athātaḥ prāyaścittaviparyāsaḥsarvatra jalābhyāsaḥ prājāpatyaṃ yatkusīdaṃ ca saṃpūtyardhyāśabaliṃ hutvā yadi purastātta viparyāso yatkusīdaṃ juhuyāt yatsarvatra na saṃskārājyamapi yajamānaṃ hutvā tatanoṣaṃ bhavati adakṣiṇabrāhmaṇaṃ tadyajñorākṣasaṃ bhavati idmaṃ vinā yajate patati narake ubhau yajamāno brahmaṇā sarvatrāhutyā kālamanupekṣayā vipro yajñaghātakaḥ tisṛbhirbrahmaghātakaḥ tisṛbhiḥ saṃdhyākālānapekṣayā vipro jyotirghātakaḥ sarvatra pradoṣeṣvadhyāyo vedaghātaka anyāvarṇo vidyādānī gurughātakaḥ sarvatra svecchayātyāgīpitṛghātakaḥ ityete ityeteṣakhāpātikanā mātra bhāṣaṇaṃ nābhivādyamatra pathena śārśanaprekṣa iti yadi pramādākṛtvā gāyatryaṣṭa japet // KauthGS_5 //
children.translated_text: Now, the reversal of <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation). Everywhere [there should be] proximity to water. The <s>Prājāpatya</s> [penance] and 'yat kusīdam' — having completed [the rite], having offered the <s>arghya</s> (respectful water-offering) and <s>bali</s> (food-offering), if there is a reversal beforehand, one should offer [with] 'yat kusīdam.' Wherever there is no consecrated ghee for the ritual, having offered [in place of] the sacrificer, that becomes sinful. Without a worthy <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [to receive] the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee), that sacrifice becomes <s>rākṣasa</s> (demonic). One who sacrifices without fuel falls into hell. Both the sacrificer and the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [priest] — everywhere, by disregarding the proper time of the offering, the <s>Vipra</s> becomes a destroyer of the sacrifice. With three [violations], a destroyer of <s>Brahman</s>. With three [violations], by disregarding the <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight) times, the <s>Vipra</s> becomes a destroyer of light. Everywhere, study during the evening twilight [makes one] a destroyer of the <s>Veda</s>. One of another <s>varṇa</s> (caste) who gives [Vedic] knowledge [to the undeserving] is a destroyer of the teacher. Everywhere, one who abandons [duties] by his own whim is a destroyer of the ancestors. These are [those who commit] sins leading to downfall. There should be no conversation with them, no greeting, no looking at them on the path. If done inadvertently, one should recite the <s>Gāyatrī</s> eight times.

children.text: KauthGS 6:
children.translated_text: <s>Kauthuma Gṛhyasūtra</s>, Section 6:

children.text: dvibhāryāgnisaṃyogaḥ /
children.translated_text: The joining of fires by one who has two wives.

children.text: athātaḥ sarvavarṇeṣu brāhmaṇānā punarādhipatyaṃ cet pūrvaṃ gṛhyāgnerardhaṃ praṇīya tayoḥ saṃyojanārthe caturthastyāhvaḥ sāyamupakramya yajamānaḥ pūrvāgnimavarohaṇaṃ kṛtvā tatra sthaṃḍilaṃ kurvana agniṃ vo vṛdhantamiti tṛcena pratiṣṭhāpyānantarabhāryā navāgnau pātreṇādāyemaṃ stomamiti tṛcena saṃyojya pratṛcāmante caturakṣarasupāṃśu tato agniraitviti ṣaḍbhirājyam hute yajamānaṃ vācayetprāṇāyāmaṃ pariṣicyāgnaye svāhā prajāpataye svāhā punaḥ pariṣicyāgauṣūkaṃ samāropaṇaṃ vāmadevyaṃ gītvā yadi deśāntare tatra laukikāgnau kuryātpūrvavat saṃyojyāpriyādhipatyaṃ cedviśeṣo 'sti tatra tadvyākhyāsyāmo brāhmaṇānāmantraya śatāpūpamāśayatakaṃ vāṣṭau snātvālaṃkṛtya kamaṇḍalunodakaṃ gṛhītvā vanāntare gatvā tasmindeśe aśuṣkāṃ komalīṃ śubhaparṇīṃ phalavatīṃ vistārayuktaṃ prāpahnīṃ sahittāṃ etairguṇavānarkaśākhāmavalokya tatpitrārthe vedavidbrāhmaṇaṃ vicārya snāpayitvārkaśākhā na haret navāsasācchādayitvā taṃ brāhmaṇo devasya tvetyarkakanyādānaṃ varaṃ pratigṛhṇāmīti purata sthaṇḍilaṃ kurvannarkasya uttarata upaviśya tāpaṣṭo brāhmaṇārkhaśākhāṃ pariveṣṭya sarve prāṅmukodaṅmukho vā brāhmaṇas tato brāhmaṇamabhyarcya pratyeka daśadaśāpūpaṃ dadyāt śeṣamuttaratī nidhāya laukikāgniṃ pratiṣṭhāpya tataḥ samūhanādi prapadāntaṃ kṛtvedhmāṅkaṃ hutvā tato vyāhṛtibhistisṛbhiḥ hutvā agniretviti ṣaḍbhiḥ punastisṛbhiḥ tato yajamānaḥ tiṣṭhannagni pradakṣiṇa gṛhya agnirāditya sarve brāhmaṇānāmantarbhāvaḥ ditvākāśayorbahirbhāvaḥ tūṣṇīṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ kuryāt svasthānamupaviśya dakṣiṇena sahitāraṃ gṛhṇīyāt tad gṛhṇāmi ta ityupāṃśu totopariṣṭāhomaṃ samāpya śiṣṭānapūpaṃ daśakaṃ brahmaṇe dadyāt daśakaṃ svayaṃ prāśrīyāt tatrāgnau pariṣicya abhyarcya vyāhṛtibhiśca tisṛbhiḥ ājyaṃ juhuyāt tadvisṛjya tato vāmadevyaṃ viprāṇāmāśiṣo vacaḥ kanyā gṛhaṃ gacchet tataḥ punarādhipatyaṃ punarādhipatyam // KauthGS_6 //
children.translated_text: Now, regarding the re-establishment of authority among all <s>varṇas</s> for <s>brāhmaṇas</s>: first, having carried half of the domestic fire (<s>gṛhyāgni</s>), for the purpose of their union, the fourth [day] is the invocation. Beginning in the evening, the sacrificer (<s>yajamāna</s>), having descended the prior fire, making a raised altar (<s>sthaṇḍila</s>) there, should establish [the fire] with the <s>ṛc</s>-triplet beginning 'agniṃ vo vṛdhantam' ("May fire increase for you"). Immediately after, the wife, having taken [fire] in a vessel to the new fire, should join [the fires] with the <s>ṛc</s>-triplet beginning 'imaṃ stomam' ("This hymn"), whispering four syllables at the end of each <s>ṛc</s>. Then, having offered ghee (<s>ājya</s>) with the six [verses] beginning 'agniretv' ("Let fire go"), the sacrificer should be made to recite <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control). Having sprinkled around [the fire with water]: '<s>Agnaye svāhā</s>' ("Oblation to <s>Agni</s>"), '<s>Prajāpataye svāhā</s>' ("Oblation to <s>Prajāpati</s>"). Having sprinkled around again, one should perform the mounting of the <s>gauṣūka</s> (ox-cart). Having sung the <s>Vāmadevya</s> [sāman], if [moving] to another region, one should perform [the rite] there in the ordinary fire as before, joining [the fires]. If [the question is] regarding the restoration of authority for the wife, there is a distinction; we shall explain that. Having invited <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, one should prepare a hundred cakes (<s>apūpa</s>) or an <s>āśayataka</s> [offering] of eight. Having bathed and adorned [oneself], taking water in a <s>kamaṇḍalu</s> (water vessel), going to the forest, in that place one should find an <s>arka</s> (sun-plant) branch that is not dry, tender, with auspicious leaves, bearing fruit, with spreading branches, and growing in full sunlight—possessed of these qualities. Having selected and consulted a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> learned in the <s>Vedas</s> for the ancestral rite (<s>pitṛ</s>), having bathed [him], one should not cut the <s>arka</s> branch. Having covered [it] with new cloth, that <s>brāhmaṇa</s> [should recite] 'devasya tva' and give the <s>arka</s>-maiden in marriage; 'I accept the groom.' Making a raised altar (<s>sthaṇḍila</s>) in front, sitting north of the <s>arka</s>, eight <s>brāhmaṇas</s> should encircle the <s>arka</s> branch. All should face east or north, [especially] the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. Then, having worshipped the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, one should give ten cakes each to each one. The remainder should be placed to the north. Having established the ordinary fire, then performing [the rites] from the sweeping to the touching of the feet, having offered the fuel-sticks, then having offered oblations with the three <s>vyāhṛtis</s>, with the six [verses] beginning 'agniretv,' and again with the three [<s>vyāhṛtis</s>], the sacrificer, standing, should circumambulate the fire clockwise, taking [it] in hand: '<s>Agni</s>, <s>Āditya</s>, all—the inner nature of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the outer nature of earth and sky.' Silently he should circumambulate three times. Having sat in his place, with the right [hand] he should grasp [the branch] along with the star [constellation]. 'I grasp that of yours'—[reciting this] in a whisper. Then, having completed the supplementary oblation (<s>upariṣṭāhoma</s>), one should give ten remaining cakes to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, and eat ten oneself. There, having sprinkled around the fire, having worshipped, one should offer ghee with the three <s>vyāhṛtis</s>. Having released that, then [singing] the <s>Vāmadevya</s> [sāman], [receiving] the blessings of the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the maiden should go home. Thus the re-establishment of authority, the re-establishment of authority. // KauthGS_6 //

children.text: KauthGS 7:
children.translated_text: KauthGS 7:

children.text: atha ṛtukālaparokṣaṇam prathamārtavādanaḥ śuddhaḥ snātvā svastivācanaṃ śayyāgṛhamalaṃkṛtya puṣphalānvikīrya pratidiśaṃ dīpairalaṃkṛtya sugandhapaṅkena dīrghacaturasraṃ sthaṇḍilaṃ kurvan uparyukṣapatramudagagramāstīryāthopari navavāsasa prāgagrāmamāstīrya prāksiraḥ patnīṃ śayitvordhvamukhonathā jānubhyāṃ pādai vasumatyākramya tatsamīpe patis tatrābhimukho bhūtvovaśyesajastaitayo nimālabhya viṣṇuryoniṃ kalpayatviti aṣṭavāraṃ japitvāṣṭaputre bhavati skakāle patiralabhyaḥ cedanyapuruṣo na kartavyaṃ syāt ṣaḍrātro ṛtukālaḥ // KauthGS_7 //
children.translated_text: Now, the observance of the fertile season (<s>ṛtukāla</s>): from the first menstruation onward, having become pure, having bathed, [performing] the <s>svastivācana</s> (auspicious recitation), adorning the bedchamber, strewing [it] with flowers, decorating each direction with lamps, making a long rectangular raised altar (<s>sthaṇḍila</s>) with fragrant paste, spreading <s>darbha</s> grass with tips pointing north on top, and above that spreading new cloth with tips pointing east, the wife should lie down with her head to the east, face upward. Then, approaching on the knees and feet, stepping upon [the earth] with [the verse] '<s>Vasumatī</s>' ("O Earth"), the husband, facing her near that [altar], having touched both of them [with the mantra] 'vaśya-aja,' should recite eight times '<s>Viṣṇur yoniṃ kalpayatu</s>' ("May <s>Viṣṇu</s> prepare the womb")—[then] she will have eight sons. If the husband is not available at the [proper] time, no other man should be employed. The fertile period (<s>ṛtukāla</s>) lasts six nights. // KauthGS_7 //

children.text: KauthGS 8:
children.translated_text: KauthGS 8:

children.text: athāto garbhasaṃskāro maithunaṣaṣṭhe pratidinaprabhṛti yugme dine yagmāsu putro jāyoran yugmāsu putro jāyeran ayugmāsu rātriṣu striyo jāyeran iti jñātvā yadā vadhvāḥ prathamagarbho bhavati tadodarasaṃskārādvāreṇotpatsyamānāpatyasaṃskārārthaṃ puṃsavanasīmantonnayanaṃ kuryād yā kutrāciddine garbhasaṃbhavastanmāsamekaṃ gaṇayitvā tṛtīyamāsāṃstvavaśobhanaṃ tataḥ puṃsavanaṃ nāndīmukhaṃ pūrve 'hani tataḥ pare 'hanyuṣasi snātvā caturasraṃ sthaṇḍilamupalipyodagagreśi darbheṣūpaviśya dakṣiṇataḥ patnīṃ cottarato yajamānodaṅmukho brāhmaṇas tato 'gneḥ praṇayanaṃ vā vinā prātarāhutiṃ hutvā samūhanādippadānta hutvā idhmāṅgaṃ hutvā tato vyāhṛtibhiḥ tisṛbhirhutvā tato yajamānaḥ patnyā pṛṣṭhatastiṣṭhat dakṣiṇakoryarādi nābhyankamamimṛśet pumāṃsāviti brūyāt svasthānamupaviśya tatopariṣṭāddhomaṃ samāpya vadhvāṃ punaḥ snātvā yajamānaḥ puṣpākṣatānekaviṃśatiyavānnavaśūpe nidhāya gṛhītvā grāmānniṣkramay vaṭarājasamīpaṃ gatvā tatra vāsinīmupasthāyotsāhavyāpinītyadrame nityagasthiterāpitsataṃ me śriyaṃ dehi tasmānnamābhīṣṭaṃ kurvantviti puṣpākṣatairabhyarcya tasyopari yavairavakīryodagagrāṃ śākhāṃ paraśunā cchedayitvā tamoṣadhobhūmau navāntarikṣe vā gṛhṇīyād ūrdhvāgrāṃ gṛhamānīya koṣṭhamadhye maṇikadeśe vā svāsane pratiṣṭāpyaṃ tataścaturasraṃ sthaṇḍilamupalipya brūyavetkimārgaṇā prapadāntaṃ kṛtvā idhmāṅgaṃ hutvā punaśca vyāhṛtibhistasṛbhirhutvā tamoṣadhessaptabhirmukhalakanyā bhrātumato prāṅmukho peṣayitvā pratyāharantīṃ taṃ pratiṣṭaṃ navavo saśrinanakṣi japet gṛhītvā yajamānaḥ tatoṣa'gneḥ paścātpatnīṃ prākśirordhvamukhīṃ śayitvāvadhvāgnyormadhye yajamānaḥ pratyaṅmukhaḥ sāyīta punānagniriti mantreṇa dakṣiṇanāsikāpuṭe piṣṭarasaṃ pīḍayitvā niṣpoḍya piṣṭaṃ salile nidhāya vastraṃ brahmaṇe dadyāt tadrasamudare kuryāt tayoḥ svasthānamupaviśya tatopariṣṭādi samāpyala tato brāhmaṇabhojanaṃ tato brāhmaṇabhojanam // KauthGS_8 //
children.translated_text: Now, the prenatal sacrament (<s>garbhasaṃskāra</s>): from the sixth day after intercourse, from each day onward — on even days and even nights a son is born, on odd nights daughters are born — knowing this, when the bride's first pregnancy occurs, for the purpose of sanctifying the offspring to be born through the sanctification of the womb, one should perform the <s>puṃsavana</s> (rite for male offspring) and <s>sīmantonnyana</s> (hair-parting ceremony). On whichever day conception occurs, counting that month as one, after the third month the <s>puṃsavana</s> should be performed, [which is] auspicious. The <s>nāndīmukha</s> (auspicious rite) [is performed] on the preceding day. Then on the following day, having bathed at dawn, having smeared a quadrangular altar and seated [the couple] on <s>darbha</s> grass with tips pointing north — the wife to the south and the sacrificer (<s>yajamāna</s>) to the north — the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> facing north, then either kindling the fire or without it, having offered the morning oblation, having offered from the <s>samūhana</s> (sweeping) up to the <s>pariṣecana</s> (sprinkling), having offered the fuel-stick oblation, then having offered with the three <s>Vyāhṛtis</s>, the sacrificer, standing behind the wife, should touch her belly from the right side downward to the navel and say 'May there be males.' Having returned to his seat, then completing the subsequent oblation, the bride having bathed again, the sacrificer, having placed flowers, unbroken rice, twenty-one barley grains, and food in a new vessel and taken them, should go out of the village to the vicinity of a great banyan tree. Having worshipped the deity dwelling there [with the mantra] 'O you who pervade with vigor,' 'O you of eternal abode, grant me the desired prosperity, may they fulfill my wishes,' and having honored it with flowers and unbroken rice, having scattered barley over it, he should cut a branch with tips pointing north with an axe. That herb should be caught either on the ground, in mid-air, or [before it falls]. Having brought it home with tips pointing upward, it should be established in the middle of the storehouse or at the neck. Then, having smeared a quadrangular altar, having performed [the rite] up to the <s>prapadānta</s>, having offered the fuel-stick oblation, and again having offered with the three <s>Vyāhṛtis</s>, that herb should be ground by seven unmarried girls whose brothers are living, facing east, while [the sacrificer] facing east grinds it. Having taken the ground substance, the sacrificer should recite [the mantra]. Then, having laid the wife behind the fire, face up with head to the east, the sacrificer should sit between the bride and the fire facing west. With the mantra 'The purifying fire,' he should press the ground juice into the right nostril, squeeze out the ground substance, place it in water, and give the cloth to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. The juice should be applied to the belly. Having returned to their seats and completed the subsequent [rites], then feeding of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, then feeding of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. // KauthGS 8 //

children.text: KauthGS 9:
children.translated_text: KauthGS 9:

children.text: atha caturthe māsi sīmantonnayanaṃ kartavyam nāndīmukhaṃ pūrve 'hani tataḥ pare 'hanyuṣasi snātvā yajamānaḥ puṃsavanaṃ krameṇaudumbanaśākhāṃ gṛhamānīya triśvetayā ca śalalyā taṇḍulān tilamiśrān śrapayitvā laukike 'gnau sthaṇḍilasyottarato nidhāya pūrvavatprapadāntaṃ kṛtvā idhmāṅgaṃ hutvā punaśca vyāhṛtibhistisṛbhirhutvā tato yajāmānaḥ pṛṣṭhastiṣṭhan taṃ gṛhītvā audumbaraśākhāmayamūrjati vā japitvā nāsāgrameti didhyaṃnnisnāranātamunnayadantimatho yenīditeti pratipya punaḥ śalalyā gṛhītvā rākā ityeke iti pratiṣṭhāp. tūṣṇīṃ triḥ prokṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā svasthānamupaviśya tatopariṣṭāddhomānsamāpya vadha dhṛtapātrā kiṃ paśyasīti vācayitvā vāmadevya gotvā tato brāhmaṇabhojanaṃ tato brāhmaṇabhojanam // KauthGS_9 //
children.translated_text: Now, in the fourth month, the <s>sīmantonnyana</s> (hair-parting ceremony) should be performed. The <s>nāndīmukha</s> (auspicious rite) [is performed] on the preceding day. Then on the following day, having bathed at dawn, the sacrificer should follow the procedure of the <s>puṃsavana</s> and bring home a branch of <s>udumbara</s> (fig tree). Having cooked rice mixed with sesame using a porcupine quill with three white [stripes] on a domestic fire, and having placed it to the north of the altar, having performed as before up to the <s>prapadānta</s>, having offered the fuel-stick oblation, and again having offered with the three <s>Vyāhṛtis</s>, the sacrificer, standing behind [the wife], having taken the <s>udumbara</s> branch and recited 'This is vigor and nourishment,' or [another mantra], gazing at the tip of the nose, should part [the hair] upward with [the mantra] 'Now, by which, may it be praised,' and then, having taken the quill, should establish it with 'O <s>Rākā</s>' — some say thus. Having silently performed the sprinkling three times, having returned to his seat and completed the subsequent oblations, the bride holding a vessel of ghee, he should ask 'What do you see?' [She should respond], and the <s>Vāmadeva</s> [sāman] is sung. Then feeding of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, then feeding of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. // KauthGS 9 //

children.text: KauthGS 10:
children.translated_text: KauthGS 10:

children.text: atha putrasya jananakāle soṣyantīhomārabhe ekadeśapraṇayana snātvā sthaṇḍilamupalipya samūhanādi prapadāntaṃ kṛtvā idhmāṅgaṃ hutvā tataḥ śirojananakāle yātiraśvīti dvābhyāmājyaṃ hutvāsau śabde nāma brūyāt putro vārabhamavenmuniśraṣṭha pṛcchāmi tvā mitvātprivās tadenāmagrahaṇaṃ karaṇātpūrvaṃ kṛtakāni nāmāni tatkathaṃ vistareṇa tathyaṃ me brūhya aśeṣaṃ tu vyākhyāsyāmo nī karaṇā davamimamañcakaṃ nā paścānpūtrakaṃ kuryād yadi viparyāsonmāyenākṛtaṃ cetaṃ hutaṃmamarghatasmājjanavadunta yatrābhāvaḥ tyasyā prāyaścittaṃ juhuyād ava vā janana iṣvāṃte sauśabde viṣṇupradevaśarmanniti manasā kalpayan manasaṃ praviśayāsauśabde vivādabīyaṃ brūyān ko nāmāsya asau śabde nakṣatraśrayaṃ nāma kartavyam maghaṃ vā putrayorekatra yānanād yadi jātakarmādi nāpataṃ saṃskārameva kartavyaṃ nāmakaraṇādūrdhvaṃ pṛthak saṃskāraṃ svayaṃ kuryāt

jātakarma vakṣyāmi daśayanāpra iti ṣayitvā trayastriṃśadbīhīti madhusarpibhyāmekaikaṃ palamādāya ubhayatra yaśaso yaśaso 'sīti saṃyojya hiraṇyaśakalena samamaṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ anāmikābhyāṃ vā saṃgṛhya tadabhāve kuśayevā yavapiṣṭamājyadvayamākṣeti śiśaṃ prataya taṃdvasarpibhyāṃ medhāṃ ta iti tato brāhmaṇadakṣiṇā // KauthGS_10 //
children.translated_text: I shall describe the <s>jātakarma</s> (birth rite): having recited "<s>daśayanāpra</s>," [and] thirty-three rice [grains], taking one <s>pala</s> (measure) each of honey and ghee, combining both [saying] "<s>yaśaso yaśaso 'si</s>" ("you are of glory, of glory"), grasping [them] together with a piece of gold using the thumbs and ring fingers — or in the absence [of gold], with a <s>kuśa</s> grass [blade] — or with barley-flour and two [portions of] ghee, [saying] "<s>ākṣa</s>," [one should touch] the child. With the two [substances] of honey and ghee, [saying] "<s>medhāṃ te</s>" ("intelligence to you") — then [there should be] a gift (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. (KauthGS 10)

Now, at the time of the birth of a son, having begun the <s>sūṣyantī-homa</s> (oblation for the woman in labor), having drawn a portion of fire from one place, having bathed, having smeared the ground-altar (<s>sthaṇḍila</s>), having performed [the rites] from the sweeping up to the <s>prapada</s>-rite, having offered the fuel-stick oblation (<s>idhmāṅga</s>), then at the time of the emergence of the head, having offered ghee with the two [verses] beginning with "<s>yā tir aśvī</s>," he should pronounce the name at the word "<s>asau</s>" [placeholder]. [Whether it is] a son — "O best of sages, I ask you: what are the names made before the naming ceremony (<s>nāmakaraṇa</s>)?" "How [is this done] in detail? Tell me the truth completely." We shall explain: the naming ceremony should not be performed after the [placement in the] cradle. If done in reverse order through error, and if the oblation has not been offered, therefore, like the birth [rite] — where there is absence [of the proper rite], the expiation for that should be offered, or at the time of birth. At the end, at the word "<s>asau</s>," one should mentally conceive [the name] "<s>Viṣṇu-pradeva-śarman</s>" and mentally enter [it]. At the word "<s>asau</s>," one should pronounce the second [name], saying "what is his name?" At the word "<s>asau</s>," a name based on the <s>nakṣatra</s> (birth asterism) should be given. [The name] <s>Magha</s> or [another] — for twins, since they travel together, if the <s>jātakarma</s> (birth rite) and other [sacraments] have not occurred, the <s>saṃskāra</s> (sacrament) itself should be performed. After the naming ceremony, the separate sacrament should be performed by oneself.

children.text: KauthGS 11:
children.translated_text: <s>Kauthuma Gṛhyasūtra</s>, Chapter 11:

children.text: tataścandradarśam /
children.translated_text: Then the moon-viewing [ceremony for the newborn].

children.text: jananādi daśarātrātpare dve vā tasminnakṣatre taṃ kumāraṃ syātitātaṃ vetadūrdhakimāṃsuśadarśanaṃ tadabhāvaṃ darśanaṃ kṛtvā cāma kuryāt kathaṃ vakṣyāmi nāndomukhaṃ pūrva'hani tataḥ ahanyuṣasi snātvā yajamānaścaturasraṃ sthaṇḍilamupalipya gṛhyāgnerekadeśāgni vibhajya samūhanādi prapadāntaṃ kṛtvā idhmāṅgaṃ hutvā tato mātā svakumāramādāyāhatena vāsā parighāya dakṣiṇataḥ pratyaṅmukhaḥ upaviśya tatkārayitvā patihaste pradāya pṛṣṭhato gatvottarato upaviśya yajamānasvaṃ kumāraṃ avalokya vyāhṛtibhistisṛbhirhutvā punaḥ pradāya yajamāno paṃcāṃ madhyena ko 'sīti dvābhyāmarakṣaṇā pratinetramabhimṛśet katamo 'sīti caturakṣareṇa śrotrābhyāṃ eṣo 'sīti tryakṣareṇa nāsāgre madhyamūlamabhimṛśed amṛtosīti caturakṣareṇa pāṇibāhubhyāṃ pratyekamabhimṛśed amṛtosīti caturakṣareṇa pāṇibāhubhyāṃ pratyekamabhimṛśya śeṣeṇa mastakaṃ gṛhītvā tato mātā ca vāmahastena kumāryavakaṃ gṛhitvā pūrvoktamākhyānaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ śravaṇe upāṃśu brūyāt tato yajamāno dakṣiṇaṃ gṛhṇīyāt tata upāṃśu sarvānhetyativādanīyaṃ nāma brūyāt tata upariṣṭāddhomaṃ samāpya yathā vāmadevyaṃgītvā pativartāśiṣo vācayitvā tathā brāhmaṇabhojanam // KauthGS_11 //
children.translated_text: From the tenth night after birth, or from the second [night] — on that <s>nakṣatra</s> (asterism), [the rite for] that infant should be [performed]. If that has passed, after that [period], [one should perform] the moon-viewing; in its absence, having [merely] done the viewing, one should perform the ceremony. How [this is done] I shall describe: facing north on the day before, then on that day, having bathed at dawn, the sacrificer (<s>yajamāna</s>), having smeared a four-cornered ground-altar (<s>sthaṇḍila</s>), having separated a portion of fire from the domestic fire (<s>gṛhyāgni</s>), having performed [the rites] from the sweeping up to the <s>prapada</s>, having offered the fuel-stick oblation, then the mother, having taken her own infant, having wrapped [him] in a fresh garment, should sit facing west on the southern side. Having had that done, having placed [the child] in the father's hand, having gone behind [him] and sat down on the northern side, the sacrificer, having looked upon his own infant, having offered [oblations] with the three <s>Vyāhṛtis</s> ("<s>Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ</s>"), having given [the child] back, the sacrificer should touch each eye [of the child] with the two [verses beginning] "<s>ko 'si</s>" ("who are you?") through the five [mantras] in the middle, [as] a protection. With "<s>katamo 'si</s>" ("which one are you?"), the four-syllabled [mantra], he should [touch] both ears. With "<s>eṣo 'si</s>" ("you are this one"), the three-syllabled [mantra], he should touch the tip and root of the nose. With "<s>amṛto 'si</s>" ("you are immortal"), the four-syllabled [mantra], he should touch each hand and arm individually. With "<s>amṛto 'si</s>," the four-syllabled [mantra], having touched each hand and arm, having grasped the crown of the head with the remainder [of the mantra], then the mother, holding the boy with the left hand, should whisper the aforementioned narrative softly into the right ear. Then the sacrificer should take [the child on] the right [side]. Then softly he should pronounce the name that is not to be contested by all. Then, having completed the oblation above, having sung the <s>Vāmadeva</s> [hymn], having had the blessings of the <s>Pativratā</s> (devoted wife) recited, likewise [there should be] the feeding of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. (KauthGS 11)

children.text: KauthGS 12:
children.translated_text: <s>Kauthuma Gṛhyasūtra</s>, Chapter 12:

children.text: athātaścandropasthānam śuklapakṣatṛtīyāpañcamyāṃ spatamyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe vāṣṭame vā nuvakṣyādinā kartavyaṃ syāt tṛtīye māsi ṣaṣṭhe māsi kāryaṃ pañcāṅgaśodhite dine /
children.translated_text: Now, then, the moon-worship (<s>candropasthāna</s>): on the third, fifth, or seventh day of the bright fortnight, or on the sixth or eighth — it should be performed according to the procedure to be stated. It should be performed in the third month or in the sixth month, on a day purified by the five limbs [of the almanac].

children.text: chandogaṃ vedavidbrāhmaṇaṃ niyakṣā sadbrāhmaṇa udayādarvāk grāmānniṣkramya saśirataṃ sthāpayitvā śaketā svarṇakalaśamādāya kāṃśya vā mṛnmayavarja jānumātramavagāhyāpo hi ṣṭhati tṛcona pūrayitvā śannī devoriti mantreṇāddhṛtyamiti śirasi vinidhāya yaḥ pāvamānoriti jalaṃ niṣkramya vāmadevyena grāmaṃ praviśet sarvatra na saṃbhāṣaṇaṃ nopahyasya sumunaso bhūtvā yajamānagṛhe devasabhāsamīpe goṣṭamadhye vā tāmudapātrāṃ cāsane nidhāyopari kuśaiḥ chādayitvā taṃ brāhmaṇayajamānādivāvabhujjan yāntī vā ityete āstamayād ahassahasirasaṃ sthāpayitvā tatra yajamānaḥ niṣkramya gṛhādbahiḥ śucau deśe caturasraṃ sthaṇḍilamupalipya dakṣiṇābhimukho bhūtvā hā u ya candreti maṇḍalaṃ praviśya prāṅmukhopaviśya svastivācanaṃ kṛtvā yajamānaṃ puṣpāñjaliṃ pūrayitvā candrābhimukhastiṣṭhan tato mātā ca kumāramuddhṛtya dakṣiṇataḥ pratyaṅmukhobhūtvā taṃ kumāraṃ pratihaste pradāya pṛṣṭhato gatvottarataḥ tiṣṭhed yajamānaḥ puṣpāñjalyuparikumāraṃ dhārayatyate sukomaṃta iti tisṛbhirupasthāyodañca mātre pradāya karābhyāmañjaliṃ kuryāt tamañjaliṃ brahmapraṇavena pūrayitvā padaścedapāñjaliṃ avasicet punastūṣṇīṃ pūrayitvā tathā dvistūṣṇīmutsṛjya pratyaṅmukhopaviśya vāmadevyaṃ gītvā tato brāhmaṇabhojanaṃ tato brāhmaṇabhojanam // KauthGS_12 //
children.translated_text: A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who knows the <s>Veda</s> of the <s>Chandoga</s> [school] should be appointed. A worthy <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, before sunrise, having gone out from the village, having placed [the child] with its head [covered], being capable, taking a golden water-pot, or a bronze one, but not an earthen one, wading in knee-deep [water], filling [it] with the <s>tṛca</s> (triple verse) beginning 'Āpo hi ṣṭhā,' drawing [the water] with the mantra 'Śan no devīr,' placing [the pot] on the head saying 'thus,' [reciting] 'Yaḥ pāvamānīḥ,' emerging from the water, one should enter the village [singing] the <s>Vāmadevya</s> [sāman]. Nowhere should there be conversation, nor should one be disturbed; being of tranquil mind, in the house of the sacrificer, near the assembly of the gods, or in the middle of the cow-pen, having placed that water-pot on a seat and covered it above with <s>kuśa</s> grasses, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and sacrificer and others should eat or go — these [activities last] until sunset, with the head-covering placed from daylight. Then the sacrificer, having gone outside the house to a clean place, having smeared a square altar, facing south, having entered the circle [reciting] 'Hā u ya Candra,' sitting facing east, having performed the benediction (<s>svastivācana</s>), having filled the sacrificer's cupped hands with flowers, standing facing the moon — then the mother, having lifted the child, facing west on the southern side, having given the child into the [father's] hands, having gone behind, should stand to the north. The sacrificer holds the child above the flower-filled cupped hands. Having worshipped with the three [verses beginning] 'Sukomanta,' having given [the child] northward to the mother, one should form an <s>añjali</s> (cupped hands) with both hands. Having filled that <s>añjali</s> with [water reciting] the sacred syllable <s>Brahma-praṇava</s>, one should pour out the <s>añjali</s> of water at the feet. Having filled it again silently, likewise having released it twice silently, sitting facing west, having sung the <s>Vāmadevya</s>, then [there is] the feeding of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>; then the feeding of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. (KauthGS 12)

children.text: KauthGS 13:
children.translated_text: <s>Kauthuma Gṛhyasūtra</s>, Section 13:

children.text: ṣaṣṭhe māsyannaprāśanam abhyūdayikam pūrve 'hani pare 'hanyuṣasi snātvā yajamāno yavapiṣṭaṃ vā pāyasaṃ śrapayitvā kriyāmakriyāmataṇḍulāṃ svarūpatvaṃ pitā tatye mātā ca kumāramādāyopaviśya jātakamavat karmārambhe pāyasaṃ prāśnoyāt tato brāhṇabhojanaṃ tato brāhmaṇabhojanam // KauthGS_13 //
children.translated_text: In the sixth month, the first feeding ceremony (<s>annaprāśana</s>) [is performed]. An auspicious [rite] on the preceding day; on the following day, at dawn, the sacrificer, having bathed, having cooked barley flour or <s>pāyasa</s> (rice pudding), [using] unhusked rice grains in their natural form — the father and the mother, having seated [themselves] with the child, as in the birth ceremony (<s>jātakarman</s>), at the commencement of the rite, one should feed [the child] the <s>pāyasa</s>. Then [there is] the feeding of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>; then the feeding of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. (KauthGS 13)

children.text: KauthGS 14:
children.translated_text: <s>Kauthuma Gṛhyasūtra</s>, Section 14:

children.text: tṛtīye varṣe vapanaṃ kāryam ābhyudāyikaṃ pūrve 'hni tataḥ pare 'hanyuṣasi snātvā yajamānaḥ caturasraṃ sthaṇḍilamupaliṣya maṇḍalādbahirdakṣiṇenā'jyāgneyādi sthāpayitvā nāpitaḥ prāṅmukhopaviśya tatoṣṇopayātrāmādarśe tadanvantaraṃ bhātkacaṃ tat paśmimena darbhaṃ piñjūlī śthaṇḍilasyottare vāyavyādi snāpayitvā raktānaḍugomayaṃ laukikatvaṃ kṛsarasthālīpāko vṛthāpakva iti homaṃ mā nāmanaśānvadeśe tato gṛhyāgniṃ pratiṣṭhāpya prātarāhutiṃ hutvā vanyagotre sarvaekadeśe kṛsalīkārayet kecittriśikhāḥ kecitpañcaśikhāḥ yathāgotrakulakalpamaraṇye keśānikhaneyuḥ taṃvinidadhatyeke māṇavakaḥ punaḥ snātvā yajamānaḥ svasthānamupaviśya athopariṣṭaḥ -maṃ samāpya vāmadevyaṃ gītvā tato brāhmaṇabhojanaṃ tato brāhmaṇabhojanam // KauthGS_14 //
children.translated_text: In the third year, the tonsure ceremony (<s>vapana</s>) should be performed. An auspicious [rite] on the preceding day. Then on the following day, at dawn, the sacrificer, having bathed, having smeared a square altar, having established [the fires] beginning with the <s>Ājya</s> and <s>Āgneya</s> [offerings] to the south outside the circle, the barber should sit facing east. Then the warm water vessel is brought; a mirror after that; then a tuft of hair; to the west of that, <s>darbha</s> grass and a brush (<s>piñjūlī</s>). To the north of the altar, beginning from the northwest, having bathed [the child], [applying] red cow-dung as is customary; a <s>kṛsara</s> (rice-and-sesame) oblation cooked in a pot, freely prepared — thus the <s>homa</s> [is offered]. 'Not by name' should be spoken at that place. Then having established the domestic fire (<s>gṛhyāgni</s>), having offered the morning oblation, in every part of the family lineage (<s>gotra</s>), one should have the <s>kṛsara</s> prepared. Some [leave] three tufts, some five tufts, according to the custom of the lineage and family. The hair should be buried in the forest; some deposit [it in water]. The boy, having bathed again, the sacrificer, having seated himself in his place, then having completed the concluding [rite], having sung the <s>Vāmadevya</s>, then [there is] the feeding of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>; then the feeding of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. (KauthGS 14)

children.text: KauthGS 15:
children.translated_text: <s>Kauthuma Gṛhyasūtra</s>, Section 15:

children.text: aṣṭame varṣe brahmacaryam dvādaśasaṃvatsarādarvāgā tatrāṣṭame varṣe kuryāt smṛtyukte śubhanakṣatre tasminnahani pūrvāhṇe upakramya pūrvaṃ nāndīmukaṃ kṛtvā tataḥ puṇyāhe pūrvāhṇe upakramya pūrvanāntīmukhaṃ kṛtvā tataḥ puṇyāhe pūrvāhne ācāryaḥ sahasirasaṃ snāpayitvā vaṭoḥ sarvapanaṃ kārayitvā snātvālaṃkṛtyāhatena vāsasā paridhāya caturasraṃ sthaṇḍilamupalipya prāṅmukhopaviśya pādau kṣolanīmākramya dakṣiṇe śiṣyastadvadācārya svayaṃ dārorvā dadyāttūṣṇīṃ navopataṃ vratimuce tadvaddhiraṇye lomnā carmaṇi upavītobhūtvā tayoḥ punarācamya gṛhyāgniṃ pratiṣṭhāya vismṛtaṃ pṛcchedācāryaḥ śiṣyo nakṣatra svayaṃ nāma brūyāt tūṣṇīṃ śiṣyāñjalau nilīya tathā bhūmauśiṣyaḥ tataḥ ācāryo brūyāt tābhyāṃ hastābhyāṃ māṇavakāñjaliṃ gṛhṇīyāt devasya tvetyācāryo mantrī sūryasyeva sarvakāmeti sarvāṅge vā tato bhaikṣaṃ yācet tat bhaikṣaṃ brahmaṇe dadyāt ācāryādhīnaḥ tūṣṇīṃ tiṣṭhet tato madhyāṅge yathoktamārjanaṃ kuryāt sāyamagnikāryaṃ tato brāhmaṇabhojanaṃ tato brāhmaṇabhojanam // KauthGS_15 //
children.translated_text: The <s>brahmacarya</s> (studentship) [begins] in the eighth year, [and should be completed] within twelve years. There, in the eighth year one should perform [the initiation], on an auspicious <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion) as stated in the <s>Smṛti</s>. On that day, beginning in the forenoon, first having performed the <s>nāndīmukha</s> (auspicious preliminary rite), then on the auspicious day, beginning in the forenoon, having performed the preliminary auspicious rite, then on the auspicious day in the forenoon, the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher), having bathed [the student] along with the head, having had all the hair of the <s>vaṭu</s> (student) shaved, having bathed and adorned [him], having dressed [him] in a new garment, having smeared a rectangular altar, having seated [him] facing east, [placing] the feet upon the foot-washing [vessel], the student on the right side — likewise the <s>ācārya</s>. He himself or his wife should give silently a new [girdle] for the vow-observance; likewise golden [ornaments], with hair, upon the skin. Having become invested with the sacred thread (<s>upavīta</s>), both of them sipping water again, having established the domestic fire (<s>gṛhyāgni</s>), [reciting] the forgotten [portion] along with the <s>gotra</s> [name]... In the <s>caula</s> (tonsure), <s>upanayana</s> (initiation), and <s>godāna</s> (gift of a cow) [ceremonies], then having performed from the sweeping up to the toe-touching, having offered the fuel-oblation, then with the [wife] following, having offered with the three <s>vyāhṛti</s>s (sacred utterances), having grasped the boy with both hands, having made him recite the discipline... One should look at <s>Savitṛ</s> (the Sun) while meditating; with 'uṣṇena' one should sprinkle hot water while meditating on <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind). The boy, having filled the joined palms with the right [hand], having shaved the hair from the right side [reciting] 'āpa undantu' (may the waters moisten), having shaved [reciting] 'viṣṇor daṣṭro 'si' (you are <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s fang), one should look at the mirror; [reciting] 'oṣadhe trāyasva enam' (O herb, protect him), having washed the <s>darbha</s> grass tuft and placed it in its spot; [reciting] 'svadhite nainaṃ hiṃsīḥ' (O axe, do not harm him), joining the mirror [with the recitation] 'oṣadhīḥ'; [reciting] 'yena pūṣā,' the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s should sprinkle him. Another man, having cut once with an iron [blade], silently casting the tips of seven hairs joined with <s>darbha</s> tips upon a bull, and again beginning from 'undantu' and so forth — thus for the back and north [sides]. [Reciting] 'triyāyuṣam' (triple lifespan), having grasped the head, one should recite. Having approached that [student], one should say 'kuru' (do) to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. 'What is your name?' the <s>ācārya</s> should ask; the student should himself declare his <s>nakṣatra</s> name. Silently the student should bow into the <s>ācārya</s>'s joined hands; likewise the student [should bow] upon the ground. Then the <s>ācārya</s> should speak; with both hands he should grasp the boy's joined palms. [Reciting] 'devasya tva,' the <s>ācārya</s> [is] the mantrin; like the sun's beneficent giver, without turning back, standing facing east, standing behind the <s>ācārya</s> facing east, both touching the navel region of the student with the palm; [reciting] 'prāṇānām' to the end, 'ka' at the ... 'hura' at the chest, 'kṛsara' at the throat... with the left [hand] the left, [reciting] 'devāya tva' or [grasping] the left with the right, [reciting] 'prajāpataye tva.' And again the <s>vaṭu</s> (student), having faced east, the <s>ācārya</s> [says]: 'You are a <s>brahmacārin</s>; O such-and-such, place fuel; partake of water; perform your duties; do not sleep during the day' — the meaning is 'you are a <s>brahmacārin</s>.' One should perform one's own fire-duty, the oblation, [reciting] the <s>prāṇa</s>, fire, and <s>gotra</s>, or 'jaṭhara' (inner fire) — thus the <s>ācārya</s> should instruct what is to be done; 'so be it,' accepting that. Having offered the morning oblation, having chanted one's own <s>sūkta</s> (hymn), one should perform <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control). In one's own <s>gotra</s> or another's — in one's own <s>gotra</s> one should give a portion of Vedic [knowledge]; or in another's. Having analyzed this, in one's own <s>gotra</s>, [the fire] in the eastern direction, in a particular place — having said 'śaudam,' they know the arrangement. Having immediately placed that fire upon the sacred grass (<s>barhis</s>), then having performed from the sweeping up to the toe-touching, having offered the fuel-oblation, then having offered with the three <s>vyāhṛti</s>s while following, and again having offered with all [vyāhṛtis] combined, the boy having offered with 'agne vratapatā' (O <s>Agni</s>, lord of vows) and the following [mantras], there he should lead [the student] between the fire and the teacher. Having thus understood, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>ācārya</s> — 'stand!' — having faced east, having placed <s>darbha</s> grass with tips pointing east, having stood as a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, having filled the water vessel, having made the student join palms, having filled [the water] into the <s>ācārya</s>'s joined palms for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, having recited the mantra before the <s>ācārya</s>, one should make [the student] look at the student's joined palms. The <s>brahmacārin</s>, having performed <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, having sprinkled around and worshipped, [reciting] 'agnaye samidham' (fuel for <s>Agni</s>), should place one piece of fuel; having offered with the second [reciting] '<s>Prajāpati</s>' mentally; [reciting] 'śraddhā me dhā' (may faith be placed in me), having raised the fire, having bowed to oneself, [reciting] 'triyāyuṣam,' having taken ash with the middle and ring fingers [joined with] the thumb, [applying it reciting]: 'brahmā bindur asi' (you are the drop of <s>Brahman</s>) on the forehead, 'āyuḥ bindur asi' (you are the drop of lifespan) on the head, 'śrīr bindur asi' (you are the drop of <s>Śrī</s>) on the chest, 'śraddhā bindur asi' (you are the drop of faith) on the throat, 'medhā bindur asi' (you are the drop of intellect) at the navel, 'tejo bindur asi' (you are the drop of brilliance) at the root of the right arm, 'kāma bindur asi' (you are the drop of desire) on the left, on the back of the hand 'sarvakāma' (all desires) or on all limbs. Then he should beg for alms; that alms he should give to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. Under the <s>ācārya</s>'s authority, he should stand silently. Then at midday he should perform the prescribed cleansing; the evening fire-duty [follows], then the feeding of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s; then the feeding of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s.

children.text: KauthGS 16:
children.translated_text: KauthGS 16:

children.text: atha godānabhṛtyaṃ brūyād ācāryassvasthānamupaviśya tathā brāhmaṇorbrahmāgnyormadhye māṇavakodagreṣu ca darbheṣvācāryānugo bhūtvā dakṣiṇajānvaktamupaviśyācāryo mekhalāṃ trirāvṛttāṃ badhvā māṇavako mantraṃ vāyacitvā iyaṃ duriktādityācāryaḥ punarācamya tato māṇavakaḥ suparṇavasubhāsalo bhūtvā śobhane muhūrtenvāvīhanaṃ parasparamupanayana ācāryapa asau māṇavako upaviśya tatopariṣṭāddhomaṃ samāpya tatassāvitropradānaṃ madhyaiḥ praṇavamuñcārya tataḥ pāde pāde 'vasāya tathā dvitīye 'vasāya mukhyaṃ tṛtīye tataḥ praṇavapūrvaṃ vyāhṛtīḥ pratyekamavadhāpya omityuccaiḥ tataḥ pālāśadaṇḍaṃ dadyāt suśravaḥ suśravasaṃ metyācāryojapitvā ekamahe suśravaḥ suśravasamiti māṇavakaṃ pratigrāhya tato dakṣiṇakare dve samidho gṛhṇīyāt dharmā bhavati dharmā bhavati // KauthGS_16 //
children.translated_text: Now, one should announce the <s>godāna</s> (hair-cutting) ceremony: the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) having sat in his own place, and likewise in between [two] <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and the two sacred fires (<s>brahmāgni</s>), the student (<s>māṇavaka</s>) having sat on the tips of <s>darbha</s> grass, having become a follower of the <s>ācārya</s>, having sat down with the right knee touching [the ground], the <s>ācārya</s> should tie the girdle (<s>mekhalā</s>) thrice-wound. The student, having recited the mantra 'iyaṃ duruktāt' ("This [protects] from evil speech"), the <s>ācārya</s> should sip water (<s>ācamana</s>) again. Then the student, having become resplendent like <s>Suparṇa</s> (Garuḍa) and the <s>Vasus</s>, at an auspicious <s>muhūrta</s> (moment), [performing] the mutual <s>upanayana</s> (initiation), the <s>ācārya</s> [says] 'that student.' Having sat down, then having completed the supplementary oblation (<s>upariṣṭādhoma</s>), then the imparting of the <s>Sāvitrī</s> [mantra]: one should utter the <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ) with the middle [tones]. Then pausing at each quarter-verse (<s>pāda</s>), likewise pausing at the second, the principal [pause] at the third. Then, having placed each <s>vyāhṛti</s> preceded by <s>praṇava</s>, [reciting] 'Oṃ' aloud. Then one should give a staff of <s>palāśa</s> (butea) wood. The <s>ācārya</s>, having whispered 'suśravaḥ suśravasam me' ("O well-famed one, [grant] the well-famed to me"), the student should accept [the staff saying] 'ekam ahe suśravaḥ suśravasam' ("I am the one, O well-famed, the well-famed"). Then he should grasp two fuel-sticks (<s>samidh</s>) in the right hand. One becomes virtuous (<s>dharmā bhavati dharmā bhavati</s>). // KauthGS_16 //

children.text: KauthGS 17:
children.translated_text: KauthGS 17:

children.text: athātaḥ prāyaścittānāṃ gṛhastho brahmacāro surāpānacaṇḍālābhigamanaṃ gurutalpakabrahmahatyāgovadhaṃ suvarṇasteyaṃ duṣpratigrahaṃ parānnaṃ vainalaghutvārthe brāhmaṇasya hittīrthaṃ prāyaścittaṃ vakṣyāmīti trirātramupavāsaḥ samidhaḥ śrapayitvā tato vapanaṃ kārayitvā kamaṇgalunodakaṃ gṛhītvā saritaḥ snāpayitvā kṛṣṇagomayaṃ gṛhītvā gohṛdaye jāta sthitā bhuvanaṃ pāvanīkṛte tasmātapāvanībhūtaḥ sarvapāpakṣayaṃ kurvityanena gomayaṃ gṛhītvā adbhiḥ saṃyūya pālāśaparṇaṃ gṛhītvā dvādaśasagṛhītaṃ pūrayitvā praṇamavaśatenābhimantrya mastake 'nulipya brahmasāgniparyantaṃ homatrayaṃ sarvatrābhyastatadupahṛtapāvana pūrvavat punarabhyāsa iti vā brahmacāryamadyapānamadhuprāśanam pratyarātraṃ muktyahīna iti nopavīta digambaraṃ dvārapālanaṃ kramukṣaṇaṃ divāmaithunaṃ divā punarbhojanaṃ caṇḍālasaṃbhāṣaṇamanyatṛtamanyocchiṣṭabhojanaṃ pārvaṇaprāśanaṃ sapiṇḍīmahaikoddiṣṭaṃ teṣu punarbrahmacaryaṃ kṛtsnatvāt pramādālaghutvamiti jñāyate dharmakterna kuryāt tadabhāśvamāśrayaṅgam vitatho bhavati tasmāddharmaparo nityakusumagranthābhyāsam tathā bhūtvā tayo punarācamayay prapadāntaṃ kṛtvā idhmāṅgaṃ hutvā tato 'nvābdhāyāṃ vyāhṛtibhistisṛbhiḥ hutvāgne vratādi paṃcabhirā cāryo juhuyāt śiṣyo mantraṃ vāyayitvācāryaḥ svasthāne tiṣṭhan yuvā śiṣyaḥ prāṅmukha udbhāvaṃ jalaṃ kārayitvā pitāñjaliṃ brahma pūrayitvā ācārya ā gantre mantramutkā śiṣyāḍjaliṃ prekṣet ko nāmetyācāryo manasā pṛcchet śiṣyayo nakṣatrāśrayaṃ nāma ityupāṃśasu tayoḥ svasthānamupaviśya tatopariṣṭāddhomaṃ samāpya sāvitropradānārthe tatsaviturvṛṇīmahe sūryo devasya dhīmahi bhāno so 'haṃ saṃpracodayāt iti tūṣṇī pālāśadaṇḍaṃ dadyāt tato brāhmaṇabhojanaṃ tato brāhmaṇabhojanam // KauthGS_17 //
children.translated_text: Now, regarding expiations (<s>prāyaścitta</s>): for a householder (<s>gṛhastha</s>) or a celibate student (<s>brahmacārin</s>)—drinking liquor, contact with an outcaste (<s>caṇḍāla</s>), violating the teacher's bed (<s>gurutalpa</s>), killing a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (<s>brahmahatyā</s>), killing a cow, stealing gold, accepting improper gifts, eating another's food—for the purpose of removing the [karmic] lightness of the sin of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, we shall describe the <s>prāyaścitta</s> at the sacred ford (<s>tīrtha</s>). [There should be] a three-night fast. Having prepared the fuel-sticks (<s>samidh</s>), then having [the sinner's] head shaved, taking water in a <s>kamaṇḍalu</s>, having bathed [him] in the river, taking black cow-dung, [reciting] 'Born in the heart of the cow, established, purifying the world; therefore having become purified, may you destroy all sin'—with this [mantra], having taken cow-dung, mixing it with water, taking a <s>palāśa</s> leaf, gathering twelve handfuls, consecrating with a hundred <s>praṇavas</s> (Oṃ), anointing the head, [performing] three oblations (<s>homa</s>) up to and including [the chant to] <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Agni</s>, the purification [offering] brought everywhere as before. Or again, the practice [of expiation for]: celibacy [violations], drinking liquor, eating honey, [sins committed] during each night, [acting as if] liberated though deficient—[these require] not [wearing] the sacred thread, going naked, guarding doors, bull-breeding, daytime intercourse, eating again during the day, conversing with an outcaste, eating another's leftovers, eating at <s>pārvaṇa</s> (new/full moon) rites, <s>sapiṇḍīkaraṇa</s> and <s>ekoddiṣṭa</s> [funeral rites]. For these, [there should be] renewed celibacy, because of the completeness [of the offenses], and the negligence and lightness [thereof] is known. One who acts against <s>dharma</s> should not do so; in the absence of that [dharma], [the one who] takes refuge becomes false. Therefore, devoted to <s>dharma</s>, [one should practice] constant study of the flower-garland [of scriptures]. Having become thus, for those two again sipping water, performing [the rites] up to the touching of the feet, offering the fuel-stick oblation, then at the <s>anvādhāna</s> (fire-placing), having offered oblations with the three <s>vyāhṛtis</s>, the <s>ācārya</s> should offer with five [mantras] beginning with 'agne vrata' ("O <s>Agni</s>, the vow"). The student, having recited the mantra, the <s>ācārya</s> standing in his own place—the young student facing east—having caused water to be brought forth, filling the cupped hands (<s>añjali</s>) with the <s>brahman</s> [prayer], the <s>ācārya</s> should look at the student's cupped hands [reciting] the mantra of the one who has come. 'What is [your] name?'—the <s>ācārya</s> should ask mentally. The student [should give] the name associated with [his birth] constellation (<s>nakṣatra</s>), in a whisper. Both having sat in their own places, then having completed the supplementary oblation, for the purpose of imparting the <s>Sāvitrī</s>: 'tat saviturvṛṇīmahe sūryo devasya dhīmahi bhāno so 'haṃ sampracodayāt' ("We choose that of <s>Savitṛ</s>, we meditate upon the god <s>Sūrya</s>, may that radiant one impel me")—silently one should give the <s>palāśa</s> staff. Then feeding of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, then feeding of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. // KauthGS_17 //

children.text: KauthGS 18:
children.translated_text: KauthGS 18:

children.text: abhibhātmānaḥ sarvāṅgaiḥ pratyekasahasraṃ sthaṇḍilamupalipya ikṣudaṇjaśakaṃ kṛtvodagagramāstīryopari śiṣyopaveśanam navaśūrpaṃ śirasi nidhāya kuśaiḥ chādayitvācāryo ghaṭenāñjaliṃ pūrayitvā dakṣiṇapādenākramya yena deveti namantriya eto nvindretyabhiṣicya punaśca vāsasā paridhāya caturasraṃ sthaṇḍilamupalipya pūrvopanayanavat pravaṇaṃ kṛtvā brīhīn vā yavān vā yathācchakasthaṃḍilaṃ pūrayitvā taṃ śūrpaṃ tadupari nidhāya tathā śiṣyopaveśanaṃ pūrvoktamantreṇa payasādi śiṣyamastake 'bhiṣiñcet caturasraṃ sthaṇḍilamupalipya pūrvopayanavat praṇayanaṃ kṛtvācāryo mekhalāṃ trirāvṛttāṃ baddhvā tūṣṇīṃ śiṣyo mantraṃ vācayitvā yathoktamantreṇa yajñopavītī śarāvaṃ mārjayitvā śanno devīriti pañcaśataṃ yaḥ pāvamānīriti triḥ śataṃ eto nvindramaṣṭacatvāri samāṃ yatra śataṃ vā śatavāraṇapraṇavaṃ śatamaṣṭottaraṃ ebhirmārjayitvā punaśca yathoktamārjanaṃ kṛtvā śucau deśe sthaṇḍilaṃ vartayitvā vā kuśagrān sahasramādāya dviśatādhikaṃ vā śataṃ vibhajya śatāgraṃ śirasi nidhāya śataṃ pādatale nidhāyākramya pārśvayoḥ śataṃ śataṃ badhnīyāt urasi āpo hiṣṭheti sahasraṃ japitvā śanno devīriti dviguṇameto nvindraṃ catvāriṃśad gāyatraṃ pañcasahasraṃ praṇavamayutaṃ kṛtvā // KauthGS_18 //
children.translated_text: Having overcome oneself with all limbs, one thousand [repetitions] each, having smeared a quadrangular altar, having prepared a sugarcane mat and spread it with tips pointing north, the student should be seated upon it. Having placed a new winnowing basket on his head and covered it with <s>kuśa</s> grass, the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>) should fill the student's cupped hands from a pot, step on [his foot] with the right foot, consecrate him with the mantra 'By which, O god,' and anoint him with 'Come hither, O <s>Indra</s>.' Then, having again clothed him with a garment, having smeared a quadrangular altar, having performed as in the previous <s>upanayana</s> (initiation), having filled the altar with rice or barley as available, and having placed that winnowing basket upon it, the student should be seated likewise. With the previously stated mantra, he should anoint the student's head with milk and other [substances]. Having smeared a quadrangular altar, having performed as in the previous initiation, the teacher should tie the girdle (<s>mekhalā</s>) thrice around [the student] silently. The student, having recited the mantra, wearing the sacred thread (<s>yajñopavīta</s>), should purify the vessel with the prescribed mantra. [He should recite] 'May the waters be auspicious' (<s>śanno devīḥ</s>) five hundred times, 'He who purifies' (<s>yaḥ pāvamānīḥ</s>) three hundred times, 'Come hither, O <s>Indra</s>' eighty-four times, 'Where the equal' one hundred times, or the <s>praṇava</s> one hundred and eight times. Having purified with these, and again having performed the prescribed purification, having prepared an altar in a clean place, or having taken a thousand tips of <s>kuśa</s> grass or an additional two hundred, dividing them into hundreds — placing one hundred on the head, placing one hundred under the feet and stepping on them, tying one hundred each on the two sides, and on the chest — he should recite 'O waters, you are indeed' (<s>āpo hi ṣṭhā</s>) one thousand times. Then 'May the waters be auspicious' double that, 'Come hither, O <s>Indra</s>' forty times, the <s>Gāyatrī</s> five thousand times, and the <s>praṇava</s> ten thousand times. // KauthGS 18 //

children.text: KauthGS 19:
children.translated_text: KauthGS 19:

children.text: atho opāsanavidhiṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now we shall explain the procedure for <s>upāsana</s> (worship).

children.text: kālo 'nādeśe sāyāmāhutyupakramya prātaḥ praste tejaḥ prāptisāyamāhur yadi samasya kṛtatvāt aprāptitvāt prātadāhuḥ so 'yaṃ yāmatrāyadarvāk yathāprāptiriti tasmātsakālaprāptirbhavati divā yāmādadvāgyathoktamiti dātistasmādaprāptirbhavati pralapya māṇavakamantraṃ punargṛhotaṃ sakṛtpraṇavenābhimantrya pītvācamyāṅgulamātraṃ jalamavagāhya prāṇāyāmaṃ sahasraṃ kṛtvāpo hi ṣṭheti śataṃ japitvā śanno dīvīriti dviśataṃ yaḥ pāvamānīriti triśataṃ eto nvindraṃ caturdaśa gāyatraṃ pañcadaśa praṇavasahasraṃ ityaṣṭa teṣāṃ sumanaso jatpa punarnābhimātraṃ jale sthitā prāṇayāmaśataṃ kṛtvāpo hiṣṭheti śatam // KauthGS_19 //
children.translated_text: The time, when not specified: beginning with the evening oblation, in the morning when [the sun] has risen — they say the attainment of radiance [comes] in the evening. If it has already been done, due to the impossibility, they prescribe the morning [offering]. This is within three watches, as per attainment — therefore timely attainment occurs. During the day, from [the end of] the watch onward, as prescribed — therefore non-attainment occurs. Having recited the <s>māṇavaka</s> mantra, having taken [the water] again in the house, having consecrated it once with the <s>praṇava</s>, having drunk it and sipped water, having immersed oneself up to a finger's depth in water, having performed <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control) one thousand times, having recited 'O waters, you are indeed' (<s>āpo hi ṣṭhā</s>) one hundred times, 'May the waters be auspicious' (<s>śanno devīḥ</s>) two hundred times, 'He who purifies' (<s>yaḥ pāvamānīḥ</s>) three hundred times, 'Come hither, O <s>Indra</s>' fourteen times, the <s>Gāyatrī</s> fifteen times, the <s>praṇava</s> one thousand — these eight, with a calm mind. Then again, standing in water up to the navel, having performed <s>prāṇāyāma</s> one hundred times, [reciting] 'O waters, you are indeed' one hundred times. // KauthGS 19 //

children.text: KauthGS 20:
children.translated_text: KauthGS 20:

children.text: atha punarbrahmacaryavidhiṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now we shall explain the procedure for renewed celibacy (<s>punarbrahmcarya</s>).

children.text: ṣaṇmāsān payobhakṣaḥ samudramavahagāhya pūrvavannāndadīmukhaṃ kṛtvā tato vapanaṃ kārayitvā aṣṭo brahmaṇānniyojya aṣṭo mṛnmayeṣu dadhimadhvājyapayaḥ śarkarīdakaṃ nālikerajalaṃ puroṣaṃ gaṃgātoyaṃ etānpūrayitvāhatena vāsasā pariveśyā ā pyāyasveti kṣīrapātramabhimantrya dadhikrāviṇeti dadhipātraṃ śukramasasīti ghṛtapātraṃ madhaduścunnadhanamiti madhupātram āpo hi ṣṭheti śarkarām kayā naścitra iti nālikeram gāyatre gomūtraṃ evaṃ deveti ścarṇodapātramiti // KauthGS_20 //
children.translated_text: For six months, subsisting on milk, having immersed [oneself] in the ocean, having performed the <s>nāndīmukha</s> (auspicious rite) as before, then having had the shaving done, having appointed eight <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, having filled eight earthen vessels with curds, honey, ghee, milk, sugar-water, coconut water, rice-gruel, and <s>Gaṅgā</s> water, having covered them with new cloth — he should consecrate the milk-vessel with 'May you swell' (<s>ā pyāyasva</s>), the curds-vessel with '<s>Dadhikrāviṇ</s>,' the ghee-vessel with 'You are the bright one,' the honey-vessel with 'Sweet honey is the wealth,' the sugar-water with 'O waters, you are indeed' (<s>āpo hi ṣṭhā</s>), the coconut with 'By which, O wondrous one,' the cow's urine with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, and the sacred water-vessel with 'Thus, O god.' // KauthGS 20 //

children.text: KauthGS 21:
children.translated_text: KauthGS 21:

children.text: ityete vā vāmityuccaiḥ brūyāt pradakṣiṇena jalaṃ vīkṣyādityamādityamaśaktascet pratiyāme sakṛt ghaṭikāvasānaṃ vātāstamayād bhavati tataḥ sāya mārjayatvā kamaṇḍalunodakaṃ gṛhītvā maḍhaṃ praviśet /
children.translated_text: Having said 'Thus, these, or thus' aloud, having looked at the water and the sun clockwise — if unable, once at the end of the watch, or [the rite] extends until sunset — then, having purified in the evening and taken water in the water-pot (<s>kamaṇḍalu</s>), he should enter the monastery (<s>maṭha</s>).

children.text: prāṅmukhopaviśya tata udakaṃ pītvā netrayīḥ prakṣālyācamya tataḥ prāṇāpānau dvau tavaśyāvīyau dvau rājanaśāśāhiṇābhyāṃ gavāṃ vrate dve idaṃ viṣṇuḥ ṣaḍṛcaṃ devavratāni eteṣāṃ punaḥ punarabhyāso na tiṣṭhaṃ vāvasānaṃ na nidraṃ drācaṃ iti dvādaśarātramupavāso hyāparevādvrataṃ na yācate /
children.translated_text: Having sat facing east, then having drunk water, washed the eyes, and sipped water, then [he should recite]: <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>Apāna</s> — two, <s>Tavaśya</s> — two, <s>Rājana</s> and <s>Śāśāhiṇa</s> — by both, in the vow of cows — two, 'This is <s>Viṣṇu</s>' — the hymn of six verses, the divine vows. These should be repeated again and again; one should not stand until completion, nor sleep, and should remain awake. Thus a twelve-night fast — he does not beg during a superior's vow.

children.text: dvādaśarātra nāśroyāt ityevaṃ dvādaśarātramupavāsaḥ kṛtvātikṛtsna iti smṛtam /
children.translated_text: For twelve nights one should not listen [to worldly talk]. Thus, having performed a twelve-night fast, it is said to be complete.

children.text: yāvadbṛhaspatirbrahmā tāvatsvarge loke mahīyate na ca punarāvartate na ca punarāvartate // KauthGS_21 //
children.translated_text: As long as <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, for that long he is glorified in the heavenly world (<s>svarga-loka</s>), and he does not return again — he does not return again. (KauthGS 21)

children.text: kauthumagṛhyaṃ samāptam //
children.translated_text: The <s>Kauthuma Gṛhya</s> [Sūtra] is concluded.
